summary: This component displays a helpful/not helpful reaction system for blog articles. It fetches vote counts from an API, lets users vote, saves their choice to localStorage to prevent duplicate voting, and shows a thank-you message with updated totals after they vote.

explanations.19: This removes leading and trailing slashes from the URL path to create a clean identifier for the article — for example, '/blog/my-post/' becomes 'blog/my-post'.
explanations.23: The vote counts start as null instead of an empty object because the component only loads localStorage data after React hydrates on the client, preventing a mismatch between server-rendered HTML and the client version.
explanations.27: Voted tracks whether the current user has already voted on this article by checking localStorage; it starts null to avoid SSR hydration mismatches, then gets populated during the effect on line 30.
explanations.30: This effect runs once per unique storageKey and reads from the browser's localStorage to see if the user previously voted on this article, then updates the voted state.
explanations.35: The empty catch block silently swallows any errors from localStorage access — this is intentional because localStorage might not be available in certain environments like private browsing mode.
explanations.38: This effect fetches the current vote counts from the API whenever the slug changes, but only if a slug exists.
explanations.41: If the response status is okay, parse it as JSON; otherwise return null so the next .then() knows the request failed.
explanations.48: useCallback memoizes the handleVote function so it doesn't get recreated on every render, which matters because it's used in onClick handlers and might be passed to child components.
explanations.64: Inside the try/catch, localStorage.setItem might fail in some browser modes, so this silently catches and ignores those failures without disrupting the vote submission.
explanations.74: If there's no valid slug (page identifier), the component renders nothing because there's nowhere to send the vote data.
